authorization.description: Configuration related to the cluster RBAC settings.
authorization.rationale: This block controls cluster RBAC configuration and can grant privileged cluster-admin access to users or groups.
authorization.compliant: Only approved organisation-managed admin groups and users are configured.
authorization.non-compliant: External or unapproved admin groups or users are granted cluster-admin access.

admin_groups.description: Groups of users that can perform operations as a cluster admin. A managed ClusterRoleBinding will be created to grant the `cluster-admin` ClusterRole to the groups. Up to ten admin groups can be provided. For more info on RBAC, see https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/rbac/#user-facing-roles
admin_groups.rationale: Admin groups control privileged cluster access. Only approved organisation-managed groups should be granted cluster-admin permissions.

group.description: The name of the group, e.g. `my-group@domain.com`.
group.rationale: The group email determines which group receives cluster-admin permissions and should belong to an approved organisation-managed domain.

admin_users.description: Users to perform operations as a cluster admin. A managed ClusterRoleBinding will be created to grant the `cluster-admin` ClusterRole to the users. Up to ten admin users can be provided. For more info on RBAC, see https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/rbac/#user-facing-roles
admin_users.rationale: Admin users receive privileged cluster-admin access and should be restricted to approved organisation-managed identities.

username.description: The name of the user, e.g. `my-gcp-id@gmail.com`.
username.rationale: The username identifies a user granted cluster-admin permissions and should belong to an approved organisation-managed identity.

aws_region.description: The AWS region where the cluster runs. Each Google Cloud region supports a subset of nearby AWS regions. You can call to list all supported AWS regions within a given Google Cloud region.
aws_region.rationale: This field defines where the AWS cluster runs. It affects deployment location but does not directly control access, encryption, network exposure, or privileged permissions.

control_plane.description: Configuration related to the cluster control plane.
control_plane.rationale: The control plane manages the cluster and includes security-sensitive settings such as encryption, IAM profiles, security groups, SSH access, and subnet placement.
control_plane.compliant: Control plane uses approved IAM profiles, encryption keys, security groups, and access settings.
control_plane.non-compliant: Control plane uses unapproved IAM profiles, missing encryption, overly permissive security groups, or unmanaged SSH access.

aws_services_authentication.description: Authentication configuration for management of AWS resources.
aws_services_authentication.rationale: This block defines the AWS role assumed by the Anthos Multi-Cloud API and can affect the permissions used to manage AWS resources.
aws_services_authentication.compliant: Uses an approved AWS service role ARN.
aws_services_authentication.non-compliant: Uses an unapproved or overly privileged AWS service role ARN.

role_arn.description: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the role that the Anthos Multi-Cloud API will assume when managing AWS resources on your account.
role_arn.rationale: The role ARN determines which AWS IAM role is assumed to manage AWS resources and should be restricted to approved roles.

role_session_name.description: Optional. An identifier for the assumed role session. When unspecified, it defaults to `multicloud-service-agent`.
role_session_name.rationale: This value identifies the assumed role session for logging and traceability but does not directly grant permissions.

config_encryption.description: The ARN of the AWS KMS key used to encrypt cluster configuration.
config_encryption.rationale: Cluster configuration can contain sensitive operational data and should be encrypted using an approved AWS KMS key.
config_encryption.compliant: Uses an approved customer-managed KMS key ARN.
config_encryption.non-compliant: Uses an unapproved KMS key ARN or lacks required encryption configuration.

kms_key_arn.description: The ARN of the AWS KMS key used to encrypt cluster configuration.
kms_key_arn.rationale: The KMS key ARN controls which key protects cluster configuration and should be restricted to approved keys.

database_encryption.description: The ARN of the AWS KMS key used to encrypt cluster secrets.
database_encryption.rationale: Cluster secrets are highly sensitive and must be encrypted using an approved AWS KMS key.
database_encryption.compliant: Uses an approved customer-managed KMS key ARN.
database_encryption.non-compliant: Uses an unapproved KMS key ARN or lacks required secret encryption configuration.

kms_key_arn.description: The ARN of the AWS KMS key used to encrypt cluster secrets.
kms_key_arn.rationale: The KMS key ARN controls which key protects cluster secrets and should be restricted to approved keys.

iam_instance_profile.description: The name of the AWS IAM instance profile to assign to each control plane replica.
iam_instance_profile.rationale: The IAM instance profile controls permissions granted to control plane replicas and should be limited to approved least-privilege profiles.

instance_placement.description: (Beta only) Details of placement information for an instance.
instance_placement.rationale: This setting controls instance placement tenancy but does not directly define access, encryption, or network exposure in the current policy scope.
instance_placement.non-compliant: Unsupported or unnecessary dedicated placement setting.

tenancy.description: The tenancy for the instance. Possible values: TENANCY_UNSPECIFIED, DEFAULT, DEDICATED, HOST
tenancy.rationale: Tenancy affects instance placement but does not directly grant access or permissions.

instance_type.description: Optional. The AWS instance type. When unspecified, it defaults to `m5.large`.
instance_type.rationale: The instance type affects capacity and cost but does not directly control access, encryption, network exposure, or privileged permissions.

main_volume.description: Optional. Configuration related to the main volume provisioned for each control plane replica. The main volume is in charge of storing all of the cluster's etcd state. Volumes will be provisioned in the availability zone associated with the corresponding subnet. When unspecified, it defaults to 8 GiB with the GP2 volume type.
main_volume.rationale: The main volume stores etcd state and may contain sensitive cluster data, so encryption and approved storage settings are security-relevant.
main_volume.compliant: Main volume uses approved encryption and storage settings.
main_volume.non-compliant: Main volume uses unapproved encryption or storage settings.

iops.description: Optional. The number of I/O operations per second (IOPS) to provision for GP3 volume.
iops.rationale: IOPS affects performance and cost but does not directly control access, encryption, network exposure, or privileged permissions.

kms_key_arn.description: Optional. The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Customer Managed Key (CMK) used to encrypt AWS EBS volumes. If not specified, the default Amazon managed key associated to the AWS region where this cluster runs will be used.
kms_key_arn.rationale: The KMS key controls encryption for the main EBS volume and should use an approved customer-managed key where required.

size_gib.description: Optional. The size of the volume, in GiBs. When unspecified, a default value is provided. See the specific reference in the parent resource.
size_gib.rationale: Volume size affects capacity and cost but does not directly control access, encryption, network exposure, or privileged permissions.

throughput.description: Optional. The throughput to provision for the volume, in MiB/s. Only valid if the volume type is GP3. If volume type is gp3 and throughput is not specified, the throughput will defaults to 125.
throughput.rationale: Throughput affects performance and cost but does not directly control access, encryption, network exposure, or privileged permissions.

volume_type.description: Optional. Type of the EBS volume. When unspecified, it defaults to GP2 volume. Possible values: VOLUME_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED, GP2, GP3
volume_type.rationale: Volume type affects performance and cost but does not directly control access, encryption, network exposure, or privileged permissions.

proxy_config.description: Proxy configuration for outbound HTTP(S) traffic.
proxy_config.rationale: Proxy configuration can affect outbound connectivity and may reference sensitive AWS Secrets Manager values.
proxy_config.compliant: Uses an approved proxy secret ARN and version.
proxy_config.non-compliant: Uses an unapproved proxy secret or exposes traffic through an unapproved proxy.

secret_arn.description: The ARN of the AWS Secret Manager secret that contains the HTTP(S) proxy configuration.
secret_arn.rationale: The secret ARN references proxy configuration stored in AWS Secrets Manager and should be restricted to approved secrets.

secret_version.description: The version string of the AWS Secret Manager secret that contains the HTTP(S) proxy configuration.
secret_version.rationale: The secret version selects a version of an approved proxy secret but does not independently grant access or permissions.

root_volume.description: Optional. Configuration related to the root volume provisioned for each control plane replica. Volumes will be provisioned in the availability zone associated with the corresponding subnet. When unspecified, it defaults to 32 GiB with the GP2 volume type.
root_volume.rationale: The root volume may contain operating system and configuration data, so encryption and approved storage settings are security-relevant.
root_volume.compliant: Root volume uses approved encryption and storage settings.
root_volume.non-compliant: Root volume uses unapproved encryption or storage settings.

iops.description: Optional. The number of I/O operations per second (IOPS) to provision for GP3 volume.
iops.rationale: IOPS affects performance and cost but does not directly control access, encryption, network exposure, or privileged permissions.

kms_key_arn.description: Optional. The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Customer Managed Key (CMK) used to encrypt AWS EBS volumes. If not specified, the default Amazon managed key associated to the AWS region where this cluster runs will be used.
kms_key_arn.rationale: The KMS key controls encryption for the root EBS volume and should use an approved customer-managed key where required.

size_gib.description: Optional. The size of the volume, in GiBs. When unspecified, a default value is provided. See the specific reference in the parent resource.
size_gib.rationale: Volume size affects capacity and cost but does not directly control access, encryption, network exposure, or privileged permissions.

throughput.description: Optional. The throughput to provision for the volume, in MiB/s. Only valid if the volume type is GP3. If volume type is gp3 and throughput is not specified, the throughput will defaults to 125.
throughput.rationale: Throughput affects performance and cost but does not directly control access, encryption, network exposure, or privileged permissions.

volume_type.description: Optional. Type of the EBS volume. When unspecified, it defaults to GP2 volume. Possible values: VOLUME_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED, GP2, GP3
volume_type.rationale: Volume type affects performance and cost but does not directly control access, encryption, network exposure, or privileged permissions.

security_group_ids.description: Optional. The IDs of additional security groups to add to control plane replicas. The Anthos Multi-Cloud API will automatically create and manage security groups with the minimum rules needed for a functioning cluster.
security_group_ids.rationale: Security groups control network access to control plane replicas and should be restricted to approved groups.

ssh_config.description: Optional. SSH configuration for how to access the underlying control plane machines.
ssh_config.rationale: SSH access can provide direct access to underlying control plane machines and should be restricted to approved key pairs.
ssh_config.compliant: Uses an approved EC2 key pair.
ssh_config.non-compliant: Uses an unapproved or personal EC2 key pair.

ec2_key_pair.description: The name of the EC2 key pair used to login into cluster machines.
ec2_key_pair.rationale: The EC2 key pair controls SSH access to cluster machines and should be restricted to approved managed keys.

subnet_ids.description: The list of subnets where control plane replicas will run. A replica will be provisioned on each subnet and up to three values can be provided. Each subnet must be in a different AWS Availability Zone (AZ).
subnet_ids.rationale: Subnets determine network placement for control plane replicas and should be restricted to approved private subnets.

tags.description: Optional. A set of AWS resource tags to propagate to all underlying managed AWS resources. Specify at most 50 pairs containing alphanumerics, spaces, and symbols (.+-=_:@/). Keys can be up to 127 Unicode characters. Values can be up to 255 Unicode characters.
tags.rationale: Tags support resource identification, ownership, and cost allocation but do not directly grant access or permissions.

version.description: The Kubernetes version to run on control plane replicas (e.g. `1.19.10-gke.1000`). You can list all supported versions on a given Google Cloud region by calling .
version.rationale: The Kubernetes version can affect exposure to known vulnerabilities and should be kept within approved supported versions.

fleet.rationale: Fleet configuration registers the cluster with a Fleet host project but does not directly control cluster access, encryption, or network exposure.
fleet.compliant: Cluster is registered to the approved Fleet project.
fleet.non-compliant: Cluster is registered to an unknown or unapproved Fleet project.

membership.description: The name of the managed Hub Membership resource associated to this cluster. Membership names are formatted as projects/<project-number>/locations/global/membership/<cluster-id>.
membership.rationale: Membership identifies the Fleet association for the cluster but does not directly grant access or permissions.

project.description: The number of the Fleet host project where this cluster will be registered.
project.rationale: The Fleet host project determines registration location but does not directly control cluster access, encryption, or network exposure.

location.rationale: This field defines the Google Cloud location for the resource but does not directly control access, encryption, network exposure, or privileged permissions.

name.rationale: The resource name identifies the cluster but does not directly control access, encryption, network exposure, or privileged permissions.

networking.rationale: Networking configuration controls cluster network placement, pod and service ranges, and VPC association, which can affect isolation and exposure.
networking.compliant: Uses approved VPC and private address ranges.
networking.non-compliant: Uses unapproved VPC or address ranges.

per_node_pool_sg_rules_disabled.description: Disable the per node pool subnet security group rules on the control plane security group. When set to true, you must also provide one or more security groups that ensure node pools are able to send requests to the control plane on TCP/443 and TCP/8132. Failure to do so may result in unavailable node pools.
per_node_pool_sg_rules_disabled.rationale: Disabling managed per-node-pool security group rules can affect control plane connectivity and may require carefully approved replacement security groups.

pod_address_cidr_blocks.description: All pods in the cluster are assigned an RFC1918 IPv4 address from these ranges. Only a single range is supported. This field cannot be changed after creation.
pod_address_cidr_blocks.rationale: Pod CIDR ranges define internal pod addressing. They should be planned to avoid overlap, but they do not directly grant permissions.

service_address_cidr_blocks.description: All services in the cluster are assigned an RFC1918 IPv4 address from these ranges. Only a single range is supported. This field cannot be changed after creation.
service_address_cidr_blocks.rationale: Service CIDR ranges define internal service addressing. They should be planned to avoid overlap, but they do not directly grant permissions.

vpc_id.description: The VPC associated with the cluster. All component clusters (i.e. control plane and node pools) run on a single VPC. This field cannot be changed after creation. - - -
vpc_id.rationale: The VPC controls the network boundary for the cluster and should be restricted to approved VPCs.

annotations.description: Optional. Annotations on the cluster. This field has the same restrictions as Kubernetes annotations. The total size of all keys and values combined is limited to 256k. Key can have 2 segments: prefix (optional) and name (required), separated by a slash (/). Prefix must be a DNS subdomain. Name must be 63 characters or less, begin and end with alphanumerics, with dashes (-), underscores (_), dots (.), and alphanumerics between. **Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the annotations present in your configuration. Please refer to the field `effective_annotations` for all of the annotations present on the resource.
annotations.rationale: Annotations provide metadata for the cluster and do not directly control access, encryption, network exposure, or privileged permissions.

binary_authorization.description: Configuration options for the Binary Authorization feature.
binary_authorization.rationale: Binary Authorization controls whether workload admission policies are enforced and can prevent untrusted images from running.

evaluation_mode.description: Mode of operation for Binary Authorization policy evaluation. Possible values: DISABLED, PROJECT_SINGLETON_POLICY_ENFORCE
evaluation_mode.rationale: The evaluation mode determines whether Binary Authorization enforcement is enabled and should be set to enforce approved policy.

description.description: Optional. A human readable description of this cluster. Cannot be longer than 255 UTF-8 encoded bytes.
description.rationale: The description is metadata for humans and does not directly control access, encryption, network exposure, or privileged permissions.
description.non-compliant: Description containing sensitive secrets or credentials.

logging_config.rationale: Logging configuration affects observability and auditability of cluster components and should enable approved logging components.
logging_config.compliant: Approved cluster logging components are enabled.
logging_config.non-compliant: Logging is disabled or required audit components are not enabled.

component_config.rationale: Component logging configuration determines which cluster components produce logs for monitoring and audit review.

enable_components.description: Components of the logging configuration to be enabled.
enable_components.rationale: Enabled logging components determine which cluster logs are collected and should include approved audit-relevant components.

project.rationale: The project identifies where the resource is created. It affects placement and ownership but does not directly define access, encryption, network exposure, or privileged permissions.
